# A Level Art & Design

> **Start here:** [[classes/a-level-art-design/unit-plans/9479-course-map|Course Map]] (all four semesters)
> **Semester plans:** [[classes/a-level-art-design/unit-plans/9479-semester-1-plan|S1]] · [[classes/a-level-art-design/unit-plans/9479-semester-2-plan|S2]] · [[classes/a-level-art-design/unit-plans/9479-semester-3-plan|S3]] · [[classes/a-level-art-design/unit-plans/9479-semester-4-plan|S4]]
> **Assessment registers:** [[classes/a-level-art-design/assessments/9479-s1-assessments|S1]] · [[classes/a-level-art-design/assessments/9479-s2-assessments|S2]] · [[classes/a-level-art-design/assessments/9479-s3-assessments|S3]] · [[classes/a-level-art-design/assessments/9479-s4-assessments|S4]]

**Cambridge International AS & A Level Art & Design (9479)** at BNDS, on the **revised 2028–2030 syllabus** (first examination 2028). This is the G11 course beginning autumn 2026 (Year 1 = 2026–27, Year 2 = 2027–28). It follows on from [[classes/pre-a-level-art-design/pre-a-level-art-design|Pre A Level Art & Design]] (G10) and is graded per [[shared/bnds-assessment-framework|the BNDS framework]].

**Entry: linear A Level, June 2028.** All three components are entered in one series, so there is no separate AS award and no carry-forward step, and spring 2027 carries no Cambridge deadline. You submit at a single point, around **end April 2028**, where C1, C2 and C3 are handed in together ([[classes/a-level-art-design/unit-plans/9479-course-map|course map]], S4).

## Syllabus at a glance (2028–2030)

| | C1: Portfolio | C2: Externally Set Assignment | C3: Personal Investigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Marks | 60 → weighted 90 | 60 | 75 → weighted 150 |
| Weight | 60% AS / 30% AL | 40% AS / 20% AL | **50% AL** |
| Nature | Internally set, externally marked; selection of work over the course | Question paper, **three themes** to choose from; supporting studies + final outcome in a **15-hour supervised test** | Theme-based investigation: **2000–2500-word written discourse** integrated with a body of visual work + bibliography |

**AOs:** AO1 Record, AO2 Explore, AO3 Develop, AO4 Present. Marks per AO — C1: 15/15/20/10; C2: 15/15/15/15; C3: 20/20/25/10. Qualification weightings: AS 25/25/29/21, AL 25/25/31/19.

Areas of study: Fine art / Graphic communication / 3D design / Textiles-Fashion (these may differ per component; the same work may never go to two components). All submission is digital (no hyperlinks/QR). C1 can be carried forward alone; C3 cannot. Private candidates cannot enter. Annotation is assessed within AO3 and must be typed. Generative-AI misuse counts as plagiarism.

## Course shape (the four-semester pipeline)

Every semester runs the same **eight-stage portfolio pipeline** (foundations → recording/sustained study → exploration/artist study → development → final outcome/portfolio), with 4 Attainments as unit gates.

| Semester | Component | Plan |
|---|---|---|
| S1 autumn 2026 | **C1 Portfolio** | [[classes/a-level-art-design/unit-plans/9479-semester-1-plan\|Semester 1 Plan]] |
| S2 spring 2027 | C3 part 1 (theme → mid-point portfolio) | [[classes/a-level-art-design/unit-plans/9479-semester-2-plan\|Semester 2 Plan]] |
| S3 autumn 2027 | C3 part 2 (finish, internal submission) | [[classes/a-level-art-design/unit-plans/9479-semester-3-plan\|Semester 3 Plan]] |
| S4 spring 2028 | C2 (15-hour test in Qingming mock week) + all-component submission | [[classes/a-level-art-design/unit-plans/9479-semester-4-plan\|Semester 4 Plan]] |

Dates for S2 onward are provisional and may shift once the school publishes the calendar for those periods.

Detail across all four: [[classes/a-level-art-design/unit-plans/9479-course-map|Course Map]].

# 9479 S1 Lesson 01: Introduction and the Theme Menu

[[classes/a-level-art-design/a-level-art-design|A Level Art & Design]] · [[classes/a-level-art-design/unit-plans/9479-s1-unit-1-foundations-on-the-theme|Unit 1]] · Lesson 01 of 15 · [[classes/a-level-art-design/lesson-plans/9479-s1-lesson-02-formal-elements-on-the-theme|L02]] →

## At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| Sessions | 4 days (W1) |
| Dates | Tue 2026-09-01 → Fri 2026-09-04 |
| AO focus | AO1 Record, orientation |
| Deliverable | Committed theme with signed commitment card; source folder with first photographs; first line studies |
| Graded? | Nothing is graded in W1–W2. The day-3 diagnostic drawing is kept as your baseline, not marked. |
| Homework | Reflection, 150 words: why your chosen theme can sustain four months (due Monday) |

These dates are provisional and may shift when the school publishes the calendar for this period.

## What you will be able to do

By the end of this lesson, you can:

1. Say how the portfolio is marked and name what a top-band portfolio actually does
2. Commit to one theme from the menu against the criteria rather than by mood, and sign the commitment card
3. Open a source folder with first photographs and first line studies on your committed theme

## Goal

By Friday you will know how the portfolio is marked, have read what a top-band portfolio actually does, have committed to one theme from the menu, and have begun looking at it. The theme decision is the most consequential of the semester, and you make it against the criteria, not by mood.

## How it runs

- **Tue 09-01 — opener, no content.** Introductions, getting to know the group, why this subject, how the course runs. It closes with the semester map (five units, four attainments, and the fact that there are no spare days) and the four AOs in plain words — orientation only, no portfolio work and nothing graded. This course runs to a linear June 2028 entry: it is a two-year relationship.
- **Wed 09-02 — the portfolio day.** One finished 96/100 portfolio shown end to end, top band vs middle band two pages side by side, then portfolio reading in pairs against the AO-language worksheet. The theme menu is presented with its criteria — no choosing yet. Exit with a shortlist of two themes, one line of reasoning each.
- **Thu 09-03 — diagnostic drawing** (one observed object, pencil only; kept, not marked). Then you **commit to your theme** one-to-one against the five criteria and sign the commitment card: theme, three source locations, first shoot date.
- **Fri 09-04 — source folder setup** (one phone folder, one physical); line-study demo (continuous then structural); line studies from first-hand objects within your theme.

## Key content: the theme menu

A theme earns its place only if it passes all five criteria: (1) primary sources photographable within daily reach all semester; (2) survives four months of looking; (3) genuinely carries line, tone, texture and color; (4) opens both 2D and 3D development; (5) has a deep artist reference pool to draw from.

- **Reflections and Surfaces** — glass, water, screens, mirrors, polished metal in daily reach; distortion gives instant composition.
- **Worn and Weathered** — rust, peeling paint, cracked walls, mended objects; the strongest texture theme, excellent 3D loop into casting and relief.
- **Hands at Work** — people making and doing; figure drawing with a reason. This one needs willing subjects, so check your access before you sign off.
- **Structures of the Everyday** — the stacked, shelved and scaffolded; a line and shape powerhouse. The risk is coldness, so your annotation must carry the why.

The final list of themes will be confirmed in class.

# 9479 S1 Lesson 02: Formal Elements on the Theme

[[classes/a-level-art-design/a-level-art-design|A Level Art & Design]] · [[classes/a-level-art-design/unit-plans/9479-s1-unit-1-foundations-on-the-theme|Unit 1]] · Lesson 02 of 15 · ← [[classes/a-level-art-design/lesson-plans/9479-s1-lesson-01-introduction-and-the-theme-menu|L01]] | [[classes/a-level-art-design/lesson-plans/9479-s1-lesson-03-intention-and-composition-planning|L03]] →

## At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| Sessions | 6 days (W2–W3) |
| Dates | Mon 2026-09-07 → Fri 2026-09-11, plus Mon 2026-09-14 |
| AO focus | AO1 Record |
| Deliverable | Formal elements study set (line, tone and form, texture, color) and Recording Page 1; digital portfolio set up |
| Feeds | CS1 collected Mon 2026-09-14 — practice for A1 |
| Homework | Sketchbook: one further study per night from the theme, alternating element; ten minutes each, dated |

These dates may shift once the school publishes its calendar for this period.

## What you will be able to do

By the end of this lesson you can:

1. Work each formal element (line, tone and form, texture, color) directly on your own theme rather than in the abstract
2. Build Recording Page 1 so that it argues something rather than displays exercises
3. Set up your digital portfolio and file the study set into it

## Goal

You work the formal elements directly on your own theme, not in the abstract. By Monday you will have looked at the theme through five different instruments, and your first portfolio page can argue something. This lesson ends Unit 1.

## How it runs

- **Mon 09-07** — contour line vs structural line: two A4 line studies of the same object, different instrument; annotate which line told the truth.
- **Tue 09-08** — nine-step tonal ladder demo, then one tonal study from a theme source, charcoal. Rule: no outlines.
- **Wed 09-09** — push the tonal study: larger, darker range, further than feels safe. Failure is the point; annotate the failure and its lesson.
- **Thu 09-10** — mark inventory (six tools); surface matching: three textures from theme sources, each rendered with the mark that fits it; peers match mark to photographed surface.
- **Fri 09-11** — limited-palette mixing toward an observed color; three color studies with swatch, mixing route, color in context.
- **Mon 09-14** — read the exemplar's opening page as an argument; compose Recording Page 1 from the week's studies, selection first; set up your digital portfolio from the template. **CS1 collected.**

## Assessment

**CS1** (formal elements study set + Recording Page 1, sketchbook) is collected Mon 2026-09-14 — see the [[classes/a-level-art-design/assessments/9479-s1-assessments|full register]]. It is marked for evidence of observation and honest annotation, not polish, and returned within five working days.

# 9479 S1 Lesson 03: Intention and Composition Planning

[[classes/a-level-art-design/a-level-art-design|A Level Art & Design]] · [[classes/a-level-art-design/unit-plans/9479-s1-unit-2-recording-and-sustained-study|Unit 2]] · Lesson 03 of 15 · ← [[classes/a-level-art-design/lesson-plans/9479-s1-lesson-02-formal-elements-on-the-theme|L02]] | [[classes/a-level-art-design/lesson-plans/9479-s1-lesson-04-the-sustained-study|L04]] →

## At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| Sessions | 4 days (W3) — Unit 2 opens |
| Dates | Tue 2026-09-15 → Fri 2026-09-18 |
| AO focus | AO1 Record |
| Deliverable | Written intention; mind map; thumbnail sheet with one composition chosen and the rejections annotated |
| Feeds | CS2 collected Fri 2026-09-18 — direct practice for A1 |
| Homework | Written annotation: expand the intention to a paragraph a stranger could follow |

## Objectives

By the end of this lesson, you can:

1. State in writing what you are looking at and why
2. Open the theme wider than your first idea, evidenced on a mind map
3. Choose one composition to sustain and annotate the rejected thumbnails with reasons

## Goal

The theme becomes an investigation. By Friday you can say, in writing, what you are looking at and why, have opened the theme wider than your first idea, and have chosen one composition to sustain — with the rejections written down. Choosing and rejecting in writing is the top-band habit this lesson installs.

## How it runs

- **Tue 09-15** — two exemplar intentions read aloud (one strong, one vague); drafting frame on the board: *I am investigating / because / I will record*; write, swap, tighten — your partner strikes every empty word.
- **Wed 09-16** — mind mapping from the object outward (material, function, memory, opposite); A3 mind map, at least three branches past the first idea; circle the branch that surprised you.
- **Thu 09-17** — the thumbnail as a cheap test (5×7 cm, tone blocked, thirty seconds of decision each); six or more thumbnails from the mind map's strongest branches; squint-test pin-up.
- **Fri 09-18** — re-read your intention against the surviving thumbnails; choose one; annotate every rejection with one honest line; assemble the CS2 sheet. **CS2 collected.** Preview: the sustained study begins Sunday.

## Assessment

## Objectives

By the end of this lesson, you can:

1. Choose an artist because they solve your problem, not because you like them
2. Analyze the work, then place its meaning in context
3. Copy the method to learn it, then answer the artist in your own work so the influence is visible, not just claimed

## Goal

Choose your first artist because they solve your problem, not because you like them. The week runs the full artist study arc: analyze, understand in context, copy the method to learn it, then answer the artist with your own work. Influence must be visible in the work, not only claimed in the writing.

## Key content: artist pools, by theme

Choose from the pool for your committed theme. To swap to an artist outside the pool, make a one-to-one case.

- **Reflections and Surfaces** — Richard Estes (urban glass), Janet Fish (glass, light, still-life color), M. C. Escher (reflecting-sphere drawings).
- **Worn and Weathered** — Antoni Tàpies (matter and surface), Aaron Siskind (photographed peeling walls), Anselm Kiefer (material and memory).
- **Hands at Work** — Käthe Kollwitz (working hands and figures), Albrecht Dürer (praying-hands studies), Yoshitoshi or a contemporary craft documentary photographer as a non-European anchor.
- **Structures of the Everyday** — Charles Sheeler (industrial structure), Lyonel Feininger (architecture into geometry), Rachel Whiteread (structure into 3D casting).

## How it runs

- **Mon 10-26** — read the criteria; pools presented, two works per artist; choose and begin your analysis (composition, tone, mark, color); write your choice rationale: which problem this artist solves.
- **Tue 10-27** — meaning and context: what the work meant then, what it means for you now; writing frame for the ESL register; in peer reading, strike every sentence that could describe any artist.
- **Wed 10-28** — method study: copy a passage of the artist's method in the artist's logic; annotate what the copying taught you.
- **Thu 10-29** — personal response: work your own source through what the artist taught; exit: name the artist's fingerprint in your piece.
- **Fri 10-30** — the influence note: point at the evidence; assemble your artist pages; **CS7 collected.**

## Assessment

- **Tue 12-01** — build the Stage 6 page as a decision trail: studies, compositions, critique, tests, choice; photograph and file. Brief for the Juniors Days gap (Wed–Fri).

## Assessment

**CS9** (targeted tests + critique response, written annotation) is collected Fri 2026-11-27 — direct practice for A3 — see the [[classes/a-level-art-design/assessments/9479-s1-assessments|full register]]. Every test answers a named unresolved question.

# 9479 S1 Lesson 14: The Final Outcome

[[classes/a-level-art-design/a-level-art-design|A Level Art & Design]] · [[classes/a-level-art-design/unit-plans/9479-s1-unit-5-final-outcome-and-portfolio|Unit 5]] · Lesson 14 of 15 · ← [[classes/a-level-art-design/lesson-plans/9479-s1-lesson-13-final-plan-and-a3|L13]] | [[classes/a-level-art-design/lesson-plans/9479-s1-lesson-15-submission-week-and-a4|L15]] →

## At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| Sessions | 8 days (W16–W17) — Unit 5 opens |
| Dates | Mon 2026-12-14 → Fri 2026-12-18, then Mon 2026-12-21 → Wed 2026-12-23 |
| AO focus | AO4 Present |
| Deliverable | The final outcome, built in one sustained run and resolved to a unified surface |
| Homework | Sketchbook during W16; none over the break — the outcome finishes in class |

## Objectives

By the end of this lesson, you can:

1. Build the final outcome in one sustained run from underdrawing to surface
2. Act on the midpoint hard look while change is still possible
3. Resolve the focal areas and unify the whole surface

## Goal

The real thing, in one continuous run: underdrawing through to surface across four days, a hard look on Friday while there is still time to change things, then three days to resolve the focal areas and unify the whole. The plan from Lesson 13 governs every session; if you want to depart from it, discuss it in a conference first rather than drifting.

## How it runs

- **Mon 12-14 → Thu 12-17** — four-day build run, one continuous session: day 1 underdrawing and block-in; day 2 mid-stages (main relationships established); day 3 production; day 4 detail and surface. Each day: re-entry look, build, exit annotation against the plan.
- **Fri 12-18** — mid-production review: your piece and your plan side by side, teacher and peer pass, protocol applied, changes listed and ranked. **CS10**: write and hand in the review reflection — what changes, in what order, and why.
- **Mon 12-21 → Wed 12-23** — three-day resolve run (criteria read, date on the board: Thu 2027-01-07): day 6 focal areas; day 7 surface unity; day 8 final touches and stop — you declare the piece finished in writing.

## Assessment

**CS10** (mid-production review reflection) is collected Fri 2026-12-18 and is direct practice for A4 on Mon 2026-12-21 — see the [[classes/a-level-art-design/assessments/9479-s1-assessments|full register]].

# 9479 S1 Lesson 15: Submission Week and A4

[[classes/a-level-art-design/a-level-art-design|A Level Art & Design]] · [[classes/a-level-art-design/unit-plans/9479-s1-unit-5-final-outcome-and-portfolio|Unit 5]] · Lesson 15 of 15 · ← [[classes/a-level-art-design/lesson-plans/9479-s1-lesson-14-the-final-outcome|L14]]

## At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| Sessions | 5 days, 7 sessions (W19) — Unit 5 and the semester close |
| Dates | Mon 2027-01-04 → Fri 2027-01-08 |
| AO focus | AO4 Present, across AO1–AO4 |
| Deliverable | Photograph, sequence, edit and submit your portfolio; sit A4; reflect on the semester |
| Feeds | **A4 Thu 2027-01-07**: final portfolio, marked against AO1–AO4; no edits after. Marking window Thu 01-07 → Wed 01-20 (nine working days) |
| Homework | Reflection: the semester look-back, finished after Friday. Winter HW: three candidate C3 themes with annotated references — the [[classes/a-level-art-design/9479-c3-winter-brief\|C3 Winter Brief]] |

## Objectives

By the end of this lesson you can:

1. Photograph the outcome as the version the examiner will see
2. Sequence the whole journey so it reads in order, and cut what does not earn its place
3. Sit A4, submit with nothing edited after, and reflect on the semester

## Goal

Submission is a supervised craft, not a scramble. Monday you photograph the outcome properly, because the photograph is the version the examiner sees. Tuesday you sequence the whole journey so it reads in order. Wednesday you cut whatever does not earn its place and check every AO. Thursday it goes in, and nothing is edited after. Friday you look back.

## How it runs

- **Mon 01-04** (two beats) — photograph the outcome: rig, light, shoot, detail passes; prepare the images: crop, correct, name, file to the template.
- **Tue 01-05** — sequencing logic: read the exemplar's page order as a story; sequence your portfolio, lay out the full run order and walk it once; peer walk: where does a stranger stumble.
- **Wed 01-06** (two beats) — edit and clean: cut what does not earn its place, log every cut; final AO check: all four descriptors, in writing, signed.
- **Thu 01-07** — **A4 attainment.** Final portfolio due and submitted in session. No edits after.
- **Fri 01-08** — submission acknowledged; what happens next (marking window, grades Wed 2027-01-20, return in W21); write your semester reflection; the C3 bridge: what a Personal Investigation is, and the winter homework — three candidate themes with annotated references, set out in the [[classes/a-level-art-design/9479-c3-winter-brief|C3 Winter Brief]].

## Assessment

**Full brief** (objectives, task, instructions, rubric): [[classes/a-level-art-design/assessments/9479-s1-a4-final-portfolio|A4 Final Portfolio]].

You sit **A4** (final portfolio: the resolved outcome plus the complete supporting portfolio, sequenced and edited) on Thu 2027-01-07 — see the [[classes/a-level-art-design/assessments/9479-s1-assessments|full register]]. The sequence must read the whole journey in order without narration: theme, recording, exploration, artists, development, outcome.

## After the semester

W20 (Mon 01-11 →) is the exam window: no Art and Design classes. The End of Term Exam format for this studio course will be confirmed in class. W21 returns portfolios with one-to-one feedback Tue–Thu; grades and comments due Wed 2027-01-20. Winter vacation runs 2027-01-24 → 2027-02-21; the three C3 theme candidates open the Semester 2 consultation cycle on Mon 2027-02-22.

# 9479 S1 Unit 1: Foundations on the Theme

[[classes/a-level-art-design/a-level-art-design|A Level Art & Design]] · [[classes/a-level-art-design/unit-plans/9479-semester-1-plan|Semester 1 Plan]] · Unit 1 of 5 · [[classes/a-level-art-design/unit-plans/9479-s1-unit-2-recording-and-sustained-study|Unit 2]] →

## What this unit does

This unit opens the Component 1 portfolio work at its foundations stage: how the portfolio is marked (the four AOs), what a top-band portfolio does, and the semester's most important decision — committing to one theme from the menu against set criteria. You then work the formal elements directly on your committed theme (AO1 Record focus), so that by the end of the unit you have looked at the theme through five instruments and can build a first portfolio page that argues something.

## Dates & span

Tue 2026-09-01 → Mon 2026-09-14 (W1 → W3 Monday; 10 sessions). There are no attainment grades in W1–W2. On day 3 you do a diagnostic drawing, which sets your baseline.

## Lessons

- [[classes/a-level-art-design/lesson-plans/9479-s1-lesson-01-introduction-and-the-theme-menu|Lesson 01: Introduction and the Theme Menu]] — 96/100 exemplar briefing, the four AOs, diagnostic drawing, theme committed Thu against five criteria, first sources and line studies.
- [[classes/a-level-art-design/lesson-plans/9479-s1-lesson-02-formal-elements-on-the-theme|Lesson 02: Formal Elements on the Theme]] — line, tone-builds-form, push-to-fail, mark/surface matching, color from observation; Recording Page 1 ("a page that argues") and digital portfolio setup. Ends the unit.

## Assessment

No attainment grades in this unit. It contains one CS task: **CS1** (formal elements study set + Recording Page 1, sketchbook), collected Mon 2026-09-14 — practice toward A1. See the [[classes/a-level-art-design/assessments/9479-s1-assessments|full register]].

## Key content

- **The theme menu:** Reflections and Surfaces · Worn and Weathered · Hands at Work · Structures of the Everyday. The final list will be confirmed in class. Your theme must pass all five criteria: photographable primary sources within daily reach; survives four months of looking; carries line, tone, texture and color; opens both 2D and 3D; a deep artist reference pool to draw from. Sign-off is one-to-one, and the commitment card is physical.
- **Source rule:** "Nothing found, nothing borrowed" — every source is your own photograph or observation.
- **Standing protocols:** studio session shape (entry look → demo → sustained work with midpoint checkpoint → exit annotation; conference rota 4–5 students/day), annotation rule (record decisions, rejections and observations, not feelings), homework rule (sketchbook / annotation / reflection only, ≤30 min).

# 9479 S1 Unit 2: Recording & Sustained Study

[[classes/a-level-art-design/a-level-art-design|A Level Art & Design]] · [[classes/a-level-art-design/unit-plans/9479-semester-1-plan|Semester 1 Plan]] · Unit 2 of 5 · ← [[classes/a-level-art-design/unit-plans/9479-s1-unit-1-foundations-on-the-theme|Unit 1]] | [[classes/a-level-art-design/unit-plans/9479-s1-unit-3-exploration-and-artist-study|Unit 3]] →

## What this unit does

This is the recording / sustained-study stage, entirely under AO1 Record. You turn the theme into a written investigation (intention, mind map, thumbnails with annotated rejections), then build its spine — one long observed study carried across two days without restarting — and everything you record becomes pages an examiner could read. The unit closes with A1, the semester's first attainment.

## Dates & span

Tue 2026-09-15 → Sat 2026-10-10 (W3 → W6), split by the National Day break. This includes the Sun 2026-09-20 make-up day and the Sat 2026-10-10 make-up day (Sports Day afternoon).

## Lessons

- [[classes/a-level-art-design/lesson-plans/9479-s1-lesson-03-intention-and-composition-planning|Lesson 03: Intention and Composition Planning]] — written intention, mind map, ≥6 thumbnails, one composition chosen, rejections annotated.
- [[classes/a-level-art-design/lesson-plans/9479-s1-lesson-04-the-sustained-study|Lesson 04: The Sustained Study]] — Stage 1 page; the sustained study across a genuine two-day run.
- [[classes/a-level-art-design/lesson-plans/9479-s1-lesson-05-recording-pages-and-a1|Lesson 05: Recording Pages and A1]] — your own photography, studies brought to one standard, recording pages sequenced; AO1 self-check; A1 sat and fed back.

## Assessment

**Full brief** (objectives, task, instructions, rubric): [[classes/a-level-art-design/assessments/9479-s1-a1-recording-milestone|A1 Recording]].

You sit **A1 on Fri 2026-10-09** — the recording milestone (intention, Stage 1 pages, sustained study, supports), marked against AO1. It feeds the mid-term grades due Thu 2026-10-29. Class tasks inside the unit, each direct practice for A1:

- **CS2** Fri 2026-09-18 — intention + mind map
- **CS3** Thu 2026-09-24 — sustained-study walked check
- **CS4** Wed 2026-09-30 — recording pages build check

See the [[classes/a-level-art-design/assessments/9479-s1-assessments|full register]].

## Key content

- Your sustained-study media are assigned to you from the W1 diagnostic.
- Use the intention drafting frame (*I am investigating / because / I will record*) to start, then move past it so the writing becomes your own voice.
- Before A1 you do an AO1 self-check: band your own work, and it should land within one band of the teacher's. Self-bandings are collected and the gap tracked.
- The holiday split is deliberate: build pages before the break, review after it. Holiday homework is primary-source sketchbook recording.

# 9479 Course Map

> [[classes/a-level-art-design/a-level-art-design|A Level Art & Design]] · the whole two-year course at a glance

The course runs **C1 → C3 (across two semesters) → C2**, closing on a **linear A Level entry in June 2028**.

| Semester | When | Component | Cohort | Plan |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | autumn 2026 | C1 Portfolio | G11 | [[classes/a-level-art-design/unit-plans/9479-semester-1-plan\|S1 Plan]] · 5 units |
| S2 | spring 2027 | C3 Personal Investigation, part 1 | G11 | [[classes/a-level-art-design/unit-plans/9479-semester-2-plan\|S2 Plan]] · 5 units |
| S3 | autumn 2027 | C3 part 2 → internal submission | G12 | [[classes/a-level-art-design/unit-plans/9479-semester-3-plan\|S3 Plan]] · 4 units |
| S4 | spring 2028 | C2 Externally Set Assignment → **all-component submission** | G12 | [[classes/a-level-art-design/unit-plans/9479-semester-4-plan\|S4 Plan]] · 5 units |

**Dates:** S1 follows the [[calendar|2026-27 calendar]]. S2, S3 and S4 dates are provisional and may shift once the school publishes the calendar for those periods.

**What linear entry means for you:** all three components are entered in the single June 2028 series, so there is no separate AS award and no carry-forward step. Spring 2027 therefore carries **no Cambridge deadline** — the first and only submission is ≈ end April 2028, where C1, C2 and C3 land together (S4 wk 11).

**Course constants:** an eight-stage portfolio pipeline every semester; 4 Attainments + 8–10 Course Skills tasks per semester; homework every week (sketchbook / written annotation / reflection, ≤30 min). Theme control tightens each component — C1 from a teacher menu → C3 student-proposed and locked in writing → C2 Cambridge-set, with the teacher shortlisting 2–3 questions per student.

## S1 — autumn 2026 · C1 Portfolio

| Code | Date | Milestone | AO |
|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | Fri 2026-10-09 | Recording milestone | AO1 |
| A2 | Mon 2026-11-09 | Exploration & artist study | AO2+AO3 |
| A3 | Thu 2026-12-10 | Development | AO3 |
| A4 | Thu 2027-01-07 | Final portfolio | AO1–AO4 |

Full detail: [[classes/a-level-art-design/unit-plans/9479-semester-1-plan|Semester 1 Plan]] · [[classes/a-level-art-design/assessments/9479-s1-assessments|S1 Assessments]].

**Full briefs** (objectives, task, instructions, rubric): [[classes/a-level-art-design/assessments/9479-s1-a1-recording-milestone|A1 Recording]] · [[classes/a-level-art-design/assessments/9479-s1-a2-exploration-and-artist-study|A2 Exploration & Artist Study]] · [[classes/a-level-art-design/assessments/9479-s1-a3-development-milestone|A3 Development]] · [[classes/a-level-art-design/assessments/9479-s1-a4-final-portfolio|A4 Final Portfolio]] · [[classes/a-level-art-design/assessments/9479-s1-the-final|The Final]].

## S2 — spring 2027 · C3 part 1 (theme → mid-point portfolio)

Opens Mon 2027-02-22. Three weeks of consultation, then the theme is locked and the research paper drafts alongside the visual work. These dates are provisional and may shift once the spring 2027 calendar is published.

| Code | Date | Milestone | AO |
|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | Fri 2027-03-19 | Recording milestone, in C3 specialist language | AO1 |
| A2 | Fri 2027-04-23 | Exploration + Artist 1 | AO2+AO3 |
| A3 | Fri 2027-05-28 | Development + research paper, first full draft | AO3 + integration |
| A4 | Fri 2027-06-11 | **C3 mid-point portfolio** | AO1–AO4 |

Other fixed points: your theme is **locked in writing** by week 3; a Qingming mock week floats in early–mid April (sketchbook brief only); the research paper outline is issued mid-semester and its bibliography must be **integrated into the body of work** (a detached bibliography loses AO1 marks). The semester closes on a summer production briefing — the largest uninterrupted C3 window. Full detail: [[classes/a-level-art-design/unit-plans/9479-semester-2-plan|S2 Plan]] · [[classes/a-level-art-design/assessments/9479-s2-assessments|S2 Assessments]].

## S3 — autumn 2027 · C3 part 2

| Code | Date | Milestone | AO |
|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | Thu 2027-10-14 | Development resumed + research paper draft 2 (marked section by section) | AO3 |
| A2 | Thu 2027-10-21 | **Mock portfolio review of the whole investigation** | AO1–AO4 |
| A3 | Mon 2027-11-15 | **Final research paper** | C3 written criteria |
| A4 | Wed 2027-12-22 | **Complete Personal Investigation** — both outcomes + portfolio + paper | AO1–AO4 |

Seniors' Days remove a full week mid-semester, so A2 lands just before it as a whole-investigation mock, and that week becomes a marking and independent-production week. Week 1 opens on 1:1 summer-production reviews; the semester ends on assembly, viva-rehearsal critique, and submission QC. Full detail: [[classes/a-level-art-design/unit-plans/9479-semester-3-plan|S3 Plan]] · [[classes/a-level-art-design/assessments/9479-s3-assessments|S3 Assessments]].

## S4 — spring 2028 · C2 + submission

| Code | Date | Milestone | AO |
|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | Fri 2028-03-10 | Recording — intention, shoots, sustained studies | AO1 |
| A2 | Fri 2028-03-24 | Experiments + **two artists** + bridge piece + scale trial | AO2+AO3 |
| A3 | Fri 2028-03-31 | Complete supporting studies — **content closes here**; nothing new is taught after | AO3+AO4 |
| A4 | Fri 2028-04-21 | Complete C2 submission package (floats with the test) | — |

- **Week 1:** the ESA paper is released and distributed; the teacher shortlists 2–3 questions per student and your **choice is locked by Friday**.
- **The 15-hour supervised test runs in Qingming mock week**, unless the school sets a dedicated window.
- **≈ end April 2028: coursework marks and samples go to Cambridge** — on the linear entry, C1, C2 and C3 all land at this single deadline. The June 2028 timetable publishes ≈ Oct 2027.
- Two artists is a calibration point, not a preference: single-artist submissions sit in the middle and low exemplar bands.

Full detail: [[classes/a-level-art-design/unit-plans/9479-semester-4-plan|S4 Plan]] · [[classes/a-level-art-design/assessments/9479-s4-assessments|S4 Assessments]].

# 9479 S1 Unit 3: Exploration & Artist Study

[[classes/a-level-art-design/a-level-art-design|A Level Art & Design]] · [[classes/a-level-art-design/unit-plans/9479-semester-1-plan|Semester 1 Plan]] · Unit 3 of 5 · ← [[classes/a-level-art-design/unit-plans/9479-s1-unit-2-recording-and-sustained-study|Unit 2]] | [[classes/a-level-art-design/unit-plans/9479-s1-unit-4-development|Unit 4]] →

## What this unit does

This is the exploration and artist-study stage. In the first half you work on AO2 (Explore): twelve prescribed media experiments, evidence-based selection, and a scale trial at outcome size. In the second half AO3 opens: two artist studies chosen to solve — and then argue about — your problem, plus a bridge piece that carries the study into development. The unit closes with A2, marked against AO2 and AO3 together.

## Dates & span

Mon 2026-10-12 → Tue 2026-11-10 (W7 → W11), with the G11 Juniors Days on Wed–Fri of W10. You sit A2 on Mon of W11, and Unit 4 opens mid-week after the feedback day.

## Lessons

- [[classes/a-level-art-design/lesson-plans/9479-s1-lesson-06-media-exploration|Lesson 06: Media Exploration]] — the twelve prescribed experiments as one three-day run; keep-or-change decided with evidence.
- [[classes/a-level-art-design/lesson-plans/9479-s1-lesson-07-selection-and-scale|Lesson 07: Selection and Scale]] — critique of the grids, media selected for writable reasons, scale trial (name what broke and repair it — that is your AO2 evidence), Stage 3 page.
- [[classes/a-level-art-design/lesson-plans/9479-s1-lesson-08-artist-study-1|Lesson 08: Artist Study 1]] — from the prescribed pool: analysis → meaning and context → method copy → personal response → influence note.
- [[classes/a-level-art-design/lesson-plans/9479-s1-lesson-09-artist-2-bridge-piece-and-a2|Lesson 09: Artist 2, Bridge Piece and A2]] — Artist 2 chosen to argue with Artist 1; bridge piece finished across the Juniors Days gap; A2 sat; one defensible direction.

## Assessment

**Full brief** (objectives, task, instructions, rubric): [[classes/a-level-art-design/assessments/9479-s1-a2-exploration-and-artist-study|A2 Exploration & Artist Study]].

You sit **A2 on Mon 2026-11-09** — exploration and artist study (twelve experiments, media selection, scale trial, artist pages, bridge piece), marked against AO2+AO3. CS tasks, each direct practice for A2:

- **CS5** Fri 2026-10-16 — experiments documented
- **CS6** Fri 2026-10-23 — Stage 3 page + selection note
- **CS7** Fri 2026-10-30 — artist pages

See the [[classes/a-level-art-design/assessments/9479-s1-assessments|full register]].

## Key content

- **The twelve experiments (prescribed):** ink+stick blind/sighted · charcoal erased back · wet-in-wet watercolor · collage from own photos · monoprint · frottage · wax resist · impasto+scraper · stippling/cross-hatch · three-media layering · low-relief maquette in raking light · digital threshold/overlay. Experiment 11 is not optional: the 2D-to-3D loop differentiates AO2 and AO3 at the top band.
- **Artist pools per theme (prescribed):** Reflections → Estes, Fish, Escher · Worn → Tàpies, Siskind, Kiefer · Hands → Kollwitz, Dürer, Yoshitoshi/craft photographer · Structures → Sheeler, Feininger, Whiteread. Each pool spans period and culture and contains one 3D-capable anchor. The choice principle: "an artist who solves your problem, not one you simply like."
- The one-sentence defensible direction from the A2 feedback day is your entry ticket to Lesson 10: no direction, no composition.

Note: these dates fall in a future term and may shift when the school publishes the calendar for that period.

# 9479 S1 Unit 4: Development

[[classes/a-level-art-design/a-level-art-design|A Level Art & Design]] · [[classes/a-level-art-design/unit-plans/9479-semester-1-plan|Semester 1 Plan]] · Unit 4 of 5 · ← [[classes/a-level-art-design/unit-plans/9479-s1-unit-3-exploration-and-artist-study|Unit 3]] | [[classes/a-level-art-design/unit-plans/9479-s1-unit-5-final-outcome-and-portfolio|Unit 5]] →

## What this unit does

This is the development stage, assessed under AO3 Develop. You build two full compositions — first your chosen direction, then a genuine alternative you reject — and critique both against your intention. Targeted tests answer only what the critique left unresolved. The unit ends by planning your final outcome completely, then reviewing the whole development trail at A3. AO3 closes into AO4 in the final lesson.

## Dates & span

Wed 2026-11-11 → Fri 2026-12-11 (W11 → W15), around the second G11 Juniors Days block (Wed–Fri of W14).

## Lessons

- [[classes/a-level-art-design/lesson-plans/9479-s1-lesson-10-composition-1|Lesson 10: Composition 1]] — composed from your own studies using tracing-paper overlays, built over two days, resolved and honestly photographed.
- [[classes/a-level-art-design/lesson-plans/9479-s1-lesson-11-composition-2-and-critique|Lesson 11: Composition 2 and Critique]] — the rejected alternative, built deliberately faster; a full-protocol structured critique; you change something because of what you heard.
- [[classes/a-level-art-design/lesson-plans/9479-s1-lesson-12-targeted-tests-and-direction|Lesson 12: Targeted Tests and Direction]] — targeted tests, not decoration; final direction with your rejection written in full sentences; a written evaluation; the Stage 6 page as a decision trail.
- [[classes/a-level-art-design/lesson-plans/9479-s1-lesson-13-final-plan-and-a3|Lesson 13: Final Plan and A3]] — final composition plan, solving thumbnails, palette argued from meaning; you sit A3; you amend the plan from feedback.

## Assessment

**Full brief** (objectives, task, instructions, rubric): [[classes/a-level-art-design/assessments/9479-s1-a3-development-milestone|A3 Development]].

You sit **A3 on Thu 2026-12-10** — the development milestone (compositions 1 and 2, targeted tests, written evaluation, final composition plan), marked against AO3. Two CS tasks give you direct practice for A3: **CS8** on Fri 2026-11-20 (both compositions photographed and laid out) and **CS9** on Fri 2026-11-27 (targeted tests + critique response). See the [[classes/a-level-art-design/assessments/9479-s1-assessments|full register]].

## Key content

- Keep the one-sentence direction from A2 at your desk. If your development drifts from it, you will be conferenced the same day.
- Two-day builds never restart — carrying a single piece through is the point. Composition 2's one-day build is intentional pressure: the process moves faster the second time.
- The rejection paragraph (final direction, Fri of Lesson 12) is the single highest-leverage piece of writing in your AO4 story.
- Your final plan must be clear enough that a capable stranger could begin the piece from it. Choose palette and materials for meaning, and name why.
- Documentation is taught here because it pays at submission: a bad photograph loses real marks.

# 9479 S1 Unit 5: Final Outcome & Portfolio

[[classes/a-level-art-design/a-level-art-design|A Level Art & Design]] · [[classes/a-level-art-design/unit-plans/9479-semester-1-plan|Semester 1 Plan]] · Unit 5 of 5 · ← [[classes/a-level-art-design/unit-plans/9479-s1-unit-4-development|Unit 4]]

## What this unit does

This is the final-outcome and portfolio stage, under AO4 Present. You build your final outcome in one continuous run: four build days, a mid-production review with real time left, and three resolve days (Lesson 14). Submission week then covers examiner-grade photography, sequencing your whole journey, an edit with a cut log, and A4 — the final portfolio, marked across AO1–AO4, which closes the semester.

## Dates & span

Mon 2026-12-14 → Fri 2027-01-08 (W16 → W19), with the winter break (W18) between the declared finish and supervised assembly. The late-work cutoff (≈Fri 2027-01-01) falls during the break.

## Lessons

- [[classes/a-level-art-design/lesson-plans/9479-s1-lesson-14-the-final-outcome|Lesson 14: The Final Outcome]] — four-day build (underdrawing → mid-stages → production → detail), a mid-production review while change is still possible, then a three-day resolve run ending in a written declared finish.
- [[classes/a-level-art-design/lesson-plans/9479-s1-lesson-15-submission-week-and-a4|Lesson 15: Submission Week and A4]] — photograph, sequence, edit with cut log, final AO check, submit on Thursday, semester reflection and the C3 bridge on Friday.

## Assessment

# Art Appreciation Resource Library

## Readings — assigned

| Reading | Where it lands |
|---|---|
| **John Berger, "The Eaters and the Eaten"** | The anchor of the food strand. Its opening line — *"To eat is to appropriate, to take into ourselves the lives of others"* — heads the Food and Ethics unit. Serves U3 |
| **John Berger, *Ways of Seeing*, ch. 1** | [[classes/art-appreciation/lesson-plans/art-appreciation-s1-lesson-10-berger-and-the-reproduction\|L10 Berger and the reproduction]] |
| **Walter Benjamin, "The Work of Art in the Age of Its Technological Reproducibility" (2nd version, 1936/2008)** | [[classes/art-appreciation/lesson-plans/art-appreciation-s1-lesson-11-aura-and-the-poor-image\|L11 Aura and the poor image]] — the aura half |
| **Hito Steyerl, "In Defense of the Poor Image"** | L11 — the poor-image half. The two readings are read against each other |
| **Susan Sontag, "In Plato's Cave"** | [[classes/art-appreciation/lesson-plans/art-appreciation-s1-lesson-12-photography-and-after\|L12 Photography and after]]. This is *On Photography*'s first essay, extracted — the full book is on the reference shelf |
| **Dean Kissick, "The Painted Protest"** · **"Hello Darkness"** | Contemporary art-world criticism; fits [[classes/art-appreciation/lesson-plans/art-appreciation-s1-lesson-13-the-artworld-and-the-brief\|L13 The artworld and the brief]] |

## Further reading

| Reading | Note |
|---|---|
| **Michael Baxandall, *Painting and Experience in Fifteenth-Century Italy*** | The source of "painting is a deposit of a social relationship." Underpins the patronage strand |
| **Francis Haskell, *Patrons and Painters: Art and Society in Baroque Italy*** | Baroque patronage. A 25-page extract (pp. 120–145) is the teaching text; the full book is the shelf copy |
| **Sarah Thornton, *Seven Days in the Art World*** | Ethnography of the contemporary art world — the empirical counterpart to Danto's philosophy at L13 |
| **Susan Sontag, *On Photography*** (full) | The complete book; "In Plato's Cave" is its first essay |
| **John Berger, *Portraits*** | |
| **The Image Object Post-Internet** | Post-internet art theory; pairs with the Ulman and Horvitz videos |
| **Documents of Contemporary Art** — 16 volumes: Abstraction · Appropriation · Beauty · Documentary · Failure · Nature · Networks · Sound · Systems · The Archive · The Artist's Joke · The Cute · The Everyday · The Sublime · Time · Utopias | The Whitechapel/MIT anthology series. A **thematic shelf, not a syllabus** — each volume is an edited collection of short primary texts. Use it to source one or two excerpts when your Atlas Book theme needs theory |

The DOCA series is the most reusable resource here for the **Atlas Book capstone**: if you are working on masks and identity, or screens, or ruins, you can go to a volume rather than open search.

# Art Appreciation

> **Start here:** [[classes/art-appreciation/unit-plans/art-appreciation-semester-1-plan|Semester 1 Plan]] · [[classes/art-appreciation/unit-plans/art-appreciation-semester-2-outline|Semester 2 Outline]] · [[classes/art-appreciation/assessments/art-appreciation-s1-assessments|S1 Assessments]] · [[classes/art-appreciation/art-appreciation-resource-library|Reading list]]

This is an **elective, internally assessed** course at BNDS — no syllabus code, no external paper. It is AP-derived in ancestry and runs under the BNDS A-Level Handbook rules ([[shared/bnds-assessment-framework]]). The class is a **mixed G11 + G12 group of about 11 students** in an ESL room. The critique protocol is adapted: you write before speaking.

**Method:** "Aby Warburg's Mnemosyne Atlas: thematic and non-linear, not chronological. Units are constellations, not periods. The throughline is that the structures of the art world are accumulated conventions rather than natural laws." The three constellation assessments (A1 board → A4 synthesis → End-of-Term retrospective) are the same move at increasing scale.

**Teaching pattern:** Mon P4 (45') · Tue P6+7 (DOUBLE, 90') · Wed P1 (45') · Fri P2 (45') — four teaching days, five periods, one double, no Thursday. The four in-class attainments (essays and constellation builds) run on the Tuesday doubles.

## Semester 1

Five units across Autumn 2026-27 — detail in the [[classes/art-appreciation/unit-plans/art-appreciation-semester-1-plan|Semester 1 Plan]]:

| Unit | Weeks | Theme |
|---|---|---|
| U1 | W1–3 | Origins and Ancestral Memory (caves, survival, ritual objects, the first board) |
| U2 | W4–7 | Narrative, Myth and Allegory (storyboards; Gentileschi; **Titian vs Manet**) |
| U3 | W8–12 | Food, the Table and Ethics (*Eat Drink Man Woman*; Heda; Last Supper; Qingming scroll; Cassatt/Rosler/Weems) |
| U4 | W13–17 | Images, Mediation and Modernity (Berger; ukiyo-e; Benjamin; Steyerl; Sontag; Greenberg; Danto) |
| U5 | W19 | Semester close: the constellation retrospective (W18 is the winter break) |

**Theorist spine in teaching order: Warburg → Berger → Benjamin → Steyerl → Sontag → Greenberg → Danto.**

Major assessments:
- A1 board — Fri 2026-09-18
- A2 Titian-vs-Manet in-class essay — Tue 2026-10-13
- A3 food/table/ethics essay — Tue 2026-11-17
- A4 synthesis constellation — Tue 2026-12-15
- End-of-Term retrospective — Tue 2027-01-05 (20%)

These dates may shift when the school publishes the calendar for that period; any change will be confirmed in class.

Semester 2 is a titled 16-week outline (art market, patronage, *La Chimera*, Shanzhai, Atlas Book capstone) — [[classes/art-appreciation/unit-plans/art-appreciation-semester-2-outline|Semester 2 Outline]].

# Art Appreciation S1 Lesson 03: The First Board

[[classes/art-appreciation/art-appreciation|Art Appreciation]] · [[classes/art-appreciation/unit-plans/art-appreciation-s1-unit-1-origins-and-ancestral-memory|Unit 1]] · Lesson 03 of 15 · ← [[classes/art-appreciation/lesson-plans/art-appreciation-s1-lesson-02-what-survives-and-why|L02]] | [[classes/art-appreciation/lesson-plans/art-appreciation-s1-lesson-04-telling-it-without-words|L04]] →

## At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| Session codes | `U1·L10`–`U1·L14` |
| Days | 5 |
| Dates | Mon 2026-09-14 to Fri 2026-09-18 |
| Deliverable | A1: Unit 1 board and justification |
| Homework | Gather candidate images, 30 min/night, days 1–3 |

## Objectives

By the end of this lesson, you can:

1. Justify every adjacency with a reason that could not be moved to a different pair
2. Arrange the panel so that the argument is legible from the layout before anyone reads a word
3. Say what an object did, not only what it showed

## Goal

The board is the course in miniature. What separates a real board from a mood board is the justification, so the adjacencies must each carry a reason. Do not start arranging before you have gathered enough candidate images — if you begin early, you arrange only what you happen to have.

## How it runs

- **Day 1 · Mon 14 Sept · `U1·L10`** — Neolithic: settlement and the made object. What changes in images when people stop moving.
- **Day 2 · Tue 15 Sept · `U1·L11`** — ritual objects and ancestral presence: what an object *does*, not only what it depicts.
- **Day 3 · Wed 16 Sept · `U1·L12`** — constellation workshop: two unlike images, one defended pairing, out loud, everybody. Direct practice for A1.
- **Day 4 · Thu 17 Sept · `U1·L13`** — build the Unit 1 board on the wall; nothing is fixed today.
- **Day 5 · Fri 18 Sept · `U1·L14`** — final hang (20 min), justification written (20 min). **A1 collected. Boards stay up.**

## Assessment

**Full brief** (objectives, task, instructions, rubric): [[classes/art-appreciation/assessments/art-appreciation-s1-a1-unit-1-board|A1 The Unit 1 Board]].

- **A1 sits Fri 2026-09-18** — Unit 1 board and justification. The criteria sheet is issued with the announcement on Fri 2026-09-04, not on the day. Marked on: every adjacency justified with a reason that could not be moved to a different pair; argument legible from the layout before a word is read; objects described by what they do.
- The grade combines a group board with an individual write-up, so half of it is collective.

# Art Appreciation S1 Lesson 02: What Survives, and Why

[[classes/art-appreciation/art-appreciation|Art Appreciation]] · [[classes/art-appreciation/unit-plans/art-appreciation-s1-unit-1-origins-and-ancestral-memory|Unit 1]] · Lesson 02 of 15 · ← [[classes/art-appreciation/lesson-plans/art-appreciation-s1-lesson-01-opening-the-atlas|L01]] | [[classes/art-appreciation/lesson-plans/art-appreciation-s1-lesson-03-the-first-board|L03]] →

## At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| Session codes | `U1·L4`–`U1·L9` |
| Days | 6 |
| Dates | Fri 2026-09-04 to Fri 2026-09-11 |
| Deliverable | One-page panel reading, plus LB1 |
| Feeds | A1 |
| Homework | Chauvet reading, 30 min, set day 2, due day 4 |

## Objectives

By the end of this lesson, you can:

1. Say what had to happen, physically, for a mark made 30,000 years ago to be in front of you
2. Read two images by proximity and say what the pairing argues, not what each one shows separately
3. Change a position in seminar when someone is right, out loud, and say that is what happened

## Goal

A1 is announced in the first ten minutes of day one, before any content, and is due Fri 18 Sept. Then five days on people who left no writing: **the wall is the evidence**, and you argue from the wall.

## How it runs

- **Day 1 · Fri 4 Sept · `U1·L4`** — **A1 announced** in the first ten minutes: the board, the justification, due Fri 18 Sept. Then: what survives, and why — name what had to happen for an object to reach you at all.
- **Day 2 · Mon 7 Sept · `U1·L5`** — Lascaux and Chauvet, first pass, no commentary; describe round. Chauvet reading set.
- **Day 3 · Tue 8 Sept · `U1·L6`** — hands, animals and the dark: account for the choice of animal, wall, and depth.
- **Day 4 · Wed 9 Sept · `U1·L7`** — why make a mark: one reason argued, evidenced from the wall.
- **Day 5 · Thu 10 Sept · `U1·L8`** — read a cave wall the way Warburg read a panel, by proximity. Two paired images; the written panel reading is the deliverable.
- **Day 6 · Fri 11 Sept · `U1·L9`** — seminar: what the first images wanted. Thirty minutes; LB1 posted from what happens inside it.

## Assessment

- **LB1** — Fri 2026-09-11, posted from the seminar. Graded on whether you took a position and moved it — a behavior, so this is what is being watched.
- **One-page panel reading** (day 5) — direct rehearsal for the A1 justification, the same move at greater length. Details will be confirmed in class.

# Art Appreciation S1 Lesson 01: Opening the Atlas

[[classes/art-appreciation/art-appreciation|Art Appreciation]] · [[classes/art-appreciation/unit-plans/art-appreciation-s1-unit-1-origins-and-ancestral-memory|Unit 1]] · Lesson 01 of 15 · [[classes/art-appreciation/lesson-plans/art-appreciation-s1-lesson-02-what-survives-and-why|L02]] →

## At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| Session codes | `U1·L1`–`U1·L3` |
| Days | 3 |
| Dates | Tue 2026-09-01 to Fri 2026-09-04 |
| Deliverable | CS1 darkroom reflection |
| Feeds | A1 |

## What you will be able to do

By the end of this lesson, you can:

1. Say why the course is arranged by resemblance rather than by date
2. Describe an image for a full minute without interpreting it once
3. Name a physical decision in your darkroom reflection, rather than a feeling about the result

## About these three days

The aim across these three days is to look before you explain. This course is arranged by resemblance, not as a timeline. The darkroom session on day three is where an image stops being a screen and becomes a thing that light did to a surface — a distinction that matters again in Unit 4 in December.

## How it runs

- **Day 1 · Tue 1 Sept · `U1·L1`** — **First half:** first session opener — introductions, getting to know the group, why this subject, and how the course runs. **Second half:** the atlas method and how you are marked — Warburg's panels and why resemblance beats date, and the course map with the four majors and the retrospective on one sheet. Close: name one thing about this course that sounds wrong to you.
- **Day 2 · Wed 2 Sept · `U1·L2`** — look before you explain. Ten minutes silent on one image with the title withheld; a description round written for two minutes, then spoken. Close: what did someone else see that you did not?
- **Day 3 · Thu 3 Sept · `U1·L3`** — darkroom: the image as physical trace. Twenty-five minutes making, fifteen minutes writing the reflection while the print is still wet. CS1 collected at the door.

## Assessment

- **CS1** — darkroom reflection, written in the room, collected Fri 2026-09-04. Marked on naming a physical decision rather than a feeling about the result.
- No homework this first week.
- A1 is announced on Fri 2026-09-04, at the start of Lesson 02.

These dates may shift when the school publishes its calendar for this period.

# Art Appreciation S1 Lesson 06: The Table as Moral Space

[[classes/art-appreciation/art-appreciation|Art Appreciation]] · [[classes/art-appreciation/unit-plans/art-appreciation-s1-unit-3-food-the-table-and-ethics|Unit 3]] · Lesson 06 of 15 · ← [[classes/art-appreciation/lesson-plans/art-appreciation-s1-lesson-05-titian-to-manet|L05]] | [[classes/art-appreciation/lesson-plans/art-appreciation-s1-lesson-07-the-split-weeks|L07]] →

## At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| Session codes | `U3·L1`, `U3·L2-3` (two-day run), `U3·L4`, `U3·L5` |
| Days | 5 |
| Dates | Mon 2026-10-19 to Fri 2026-10-23 |
| Deliverable | A written reading of one meal, plus LB3 |
| Feeds | A3 |
| Homework | Finish the film on your own if the screening runs short; otherwise none |

## What you will be able to do

By the end of this lesson, you can:

1. Treat the table as a site of enforcement, not just a setting
2. Read one meal as an argument the characters cannot make aloud, and name what the argument is about
3. Say who is fed, who serves, and who is not in the picture

## Overview

Unit 3 opens on a film because the table is easier to see when it is moving. In Ang Lee's cooking scenes, everything the family cannot say is said through food. The screening runs across Tuesday and Wednesday as one continuing session.

## How it runs

- **Day 1 · Mon 19 Oct · `U3·L1`** — the table as moral space, the frame for the whole unit; first look at three paintings of meals: who is where.
- **Days 2–3 · Tue 20 – Wed 21 Oct · `U3·L2-3`** — *Eat Drink Man Woman* screening as one two-day session: day one screens 40 minutes; day two screens 45 minutes and picks up from the cut.
- **Thu 22 Oct · `U3·L4`** — the film's table: one meal replayed twice, then your written reading — "an argument nobody can make aloud." This reading is the deliverable.
- **Fri 23 Oct · `U3·L5`** — seminar: food, class, and who is not in the picture. LB3 posted.

## Assessment

- **LB3** — Fri 2026-10-23, seminar posting.
- **Deliverable**: a one-page written reading of a single meal sequence, due Thursday, grounded in the `U3·L4` goal.

# Art Appreciation S1 Unit 1: Origins and Ancestral Memory

[[classes/art-appreciation/art-appreciation|Art Appreciation]] · [[classes/art-appreciation/unit-plans/art-appreciation-semester-1-plan|Semester 1 Plan]] · Unit 1 of 5 · next: [[classes/art-appreciation/unit-plans/art-appreciation-s1-unit-2-narrative-myth-and-allegory|Unit 2 →]]

## What this unit covers

This unit introduces the course's method: Warburg's atlas — thematic and non-linear, grouping images by resemblance rather than by date. You work from the earliest images (Chauvet, Lascaux) through Neolithic settlement and ritual objects, focusing on what an object does, not just what it depicts. You then build the first board, a small-scale version of the move you repeat later in A4 and the End-of-Term retrospective. The darkroom session on day three shows how an image is something light did to a surface, which prepares you for Unit 4 in December.

- Key theorist: Aby Warburg.
- Key material: cave imagery, Neolithic figures, ritual objects.

## Dates and span

# Art Appreciation S1 Unit 4: Images, Mediation and Modernity

[[classes/art-appreciation/art-appreciation|Art Appreciation]] · [[classes/art-appreciation/unit-plans/art-appreciation-semester-1-plan|Semester 1 Plan]] · Unit 4 of 5 · [[classes/art-appreciation/unit-plans/art-appreciation-s1-unit-3-food-the-table-and-ethics|← Unit 3]] | [[classes/art-appreciation/unit-plans/art-appreciation-s1-unit-5-semester-close-and-retrospective|Unit 5 →]]

## What this unit does

This unit works through the theorists at the centre of the course, in teaching order: Berger (a reproduction is not a neutral copy), Benjamin (aura, introduced through ukiyo-e — "a print is already many"), Steyerl (the poor image, defended and then made in the lab), Sontag (photographing as an act on the world), Greenberg (avant-garde and kitsch), and Danto (the artworld, with Warhol and Duchamp). The A4 synthesis is the second constellation of the year and builds on the darkroom work from earlier in the course. The unit's last lesson sets the retrospective brief as break homework, which counts toward Unit 5's End of Term.

# Art Appreciation S1 Unit 2: Narrative, Myth and Allegory

[[classes/art-appreciation/art-appreciation|Art Appreciation]] · [[classes/art-appreciation/unit-plans/art-appreciation-semester-1-plan|Semester 1 Plan]] · Unit 2 of 5 · [[classes/art-appreciation/unit-plans/art-appreciation-s1-unit-1-origins-and-ancestral-memory|← Unit 1]] | [[classes/art-appreciation/unit-plans/art-appreciation-s1-unit-3-food-the-table-and-ethics|Unit 3 →]]

## What this unit does

This unit is about how images carry a story without words. The first half builds your vocabulary — narrative (where a still image puts time), myth (shared shorthand that needs an audience who already knows the reference), allegory (the image that means something elsewhere), and cycle — and turns it into a made thing: a ten-frame storyboard that carries its story on framing alone.

The second half centres on a pair of works: Titian's *Venus of Urbino* (what it asks you to accept as natural) against Manet's *Olympia* (locating the exact refusals), with Gentileschi's *Judith Slaying Holofernes* as a close-looking study of the problem of the witness. You learn the critique flow — describe, account, judge — at the top of Lesson 04. The storyboard is direct rehearsal for the A2 comparison; both are about reading what a picture decided.

# Art Appreciation S1 Unit 3: Food, the Table and Ethics

[[classes/art-appreciation/art-appreciation|Art Appreciation]] · [[classes/art-appreciation/unit-plans/art-appreciation-semester-1-plan|Semester 1 Plan]] · Unit 3 of 5 · [[classes/art-appreciation/unit-plans/art-appreciation-s1-unit-2-narrative-myth-and-allegory|← Unit 2]] | [[classes/art-appreciation/unit-plans/art-appreciation-s1-unit-4-images-mediation-and-modernity|Unit 4 →]]

## What this unit does

This unit looks at the table as a place where rules get enforced, not just a setting. It opens on film — Ang Lee's *Eat Drink Man Woman* — then works through still life as inventory (Heda, the same painting two days running), Leonardo's *Last Supper* as a chosen moment, Bruegel and Steen's disorder taken seriously, and the Qingming scroll walked along its printed length. It closes on three artists the earlier paintings could not anticipate — Cassatt (domestic labour as labour), Rosler's *Semiotics of the Kitchen*, and Weems's *Kitchen Table Series* — and the A3 essay. This is the longest unit of the semester.

# 9607 S1 Lesson 01: The Four Key Concepts

[[classes/media-studies/media-studies|Media Studies]] · [[classes/media-studies/unit-plans/9607-s1-unit-1-introduction|Unit 1]] · Lesson 01 of 16 · [[classes/media-studies/lesson-plans/9607-s1-lesson-02-semiotics-how-images-mean|L02]] →

## At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| Days | 3 — Tue single, Wed double, Fri single |
| Dates | Tue 2026-09-01 · Wed 09-02 · Fri 09-04 |
| Band/Unit | U1 Introduction ([[classes/media-studies/unit-plans/9607-s1-unit-1-introduction\|S1 Unit 1]]) |
| AO focus | AO2 |
| Deliverable | CS1 analytical paragraph — denotation only, written Friday |
| Feeds | A1 (the denotation discipline is the foundation A1 is marked on) |
| Homework | D1: the 24-hour media-use log + blog set-up begun · D2: digital-identity mind map · all week: EN/ZH lexicon (≥5 entries by Friday) |

## Objectives

By the end of this lesson you can:

1. Name the four Key Concepts and apply each, orally, to a text from the opening menu
2. Explain, with one concrete example, why a media text is a version and not a window
3. Write a paragraph that contains zero interpretive claims and survives a peer challenge to find one
4. Log at least five lexicon entries with EN/ZH labels by Friday

## Goal

By the end of week 1 you own Language, Representation, Industry and Audience as working tools, not just vocabulary, and you hold the course's founding claim — **media is a version, not a window** — with three historical proofs behind it. You prove it by writing the hardest paragraph in the subject: pure denotation, every interpretive impulse held back. Describing before meaning is what A1 rewards, so you install it on day three of the course.

## How it runs

### D1 — Tue 09-01 (single): the opener and the wager

- **The opener (~30 min)** — introductions, why Media Studies, how the course runs, the two-year map in one slide. **Both EN and ZH are legitimate in the room** — the shared lexicon starts this week and lives on the wall.
- **The wager (~10 min)** — the claim on the board: *"I'm not impacted by media."* Hands up who agrees; the count is recorded and the vote re-runs in June. Then the homework that settles it: **the media-use log** (coursebook §1.1) — every media contact for the next 24 hours, however small, EN or ZH, platform and minutes.
- **Close (~5 min)** — **CS1 announced** (Friday, in class): one paragraph, describing only. Blog set-up begins as homework this week (mechanics finish at L07; today just the account).

### D2 — Wed 09-02 (double): the four tools and the mediation demo

- **Starter (10 min)** — media-use logs on tables; the room's 24 hours are tallied by platform. The wager revisited: *not impacted?* The evidence says otherwise — and everyone here is an **audience** before anything else. First concept named from your own data.
- **Teach: the four Key Concepts (20 min)** — one shared text from the opening menu, read four times through four lenses, pairs applying each concept orally before writing: **Language** (how it is made to mean), **Representation** (how people, places and ideas are shown), **Industry** (who made it, and why), **Audience** (who it is for, and what they do with it). Board anchors stay up all semester.
- **The mediation demo (20 min)** — *a version, not a window*, proven three times over a century before Photoshop:
 - **Staging** — Gardner's *Home of a Rebel Sharpshooter* (1863): the most famous photograph of the American Civil War, and the soldier's body was **moved and posed** for the composition, rifle propped by the photographer. Arranged before the shutter opened.
 - **Selection** — Lange's *Migrant Mother* (1936): one frame chosen from six exposures, cropped, a distracting thumb later retouched away. Every photograph is the frames not chosen.
 - **Anchorage** — an Underwood & Underwood stereograph (c. 1917): three women watch soldiers march away, and the caption — *"Mother, Wife, and Sweetheart…"* — tells you who they are and how to feel. The words steer the image.
 Then the live turn: one staged classroom "event" photographed once, and three pairs re-crop and re-caption it into three different stories on their phones. Same event, three versions, five minutes.
- **Card sort (25 min)** — the 24 EN/ZH concept cards in threes, every placement justified aloud; at least four cards are deliberately contestable ("a WeChat sticker", "the seat you watch from"). Disagreements go on the board.
- **Review (15 min)** — the contested cards argued properly; exit line, written: *"Media is a version, not a window, because…"*
- **Homework** — **WS 1.1**, the digital-identity mind map (it feeds the L07 blog); the **WS 5.2 body map** is the more visual, lower-language alternative. Lexicon entries continue.

### D3 — Fri 09-04 (single): denotation, and CS1

- **Model (15 min)** — a denotation-only paragraph written live about *Migrant Mother*, thinking aloud about what gets **excluded**: "a woman, seated, hand at her chin; two children face away, heads on her shoulders" survives — "worried", "poor", "desperate" go on a parked list. That parked list gets its name at L02.
- **CS1 (25 min)** — a new unseen still, one paragraph, denotation only, sentence frames available: *"The image shows…" / "In the foreground / background…" / "The figure is positioned…" / "The text reads…"* — no evaluative adjectives anywhere.
- **Exit swap (5 min)** — papers trade; each reader hunts for one smuggled connotation and circles it. A paragraph that survives the hunt is the win condition.

## Assessment

| Item | Date | What | AO |
|---|---|---|---|
| CS1 | Fri 2026-09-04 | Analytical paragraph, denotation only, written in class | AO2 |

CS1 is announced on day 1, giving you 72 hours' notice. It is marked for discipline, not polish — zero interpretive claims is the criterion — and returned within five working days. See the [[classes/media-studies/assessments/9607-s1-assessments|full register]].

# 9607 S1 Lesson 02: Semiotics — How Images Mean

[[classes/media-studies/media-studies|Media Studies]] · [[classes/media-studies/unit-plans/9607-s1-unit-2-media-language|Unit 2]] · Lesson 02 of 16 · ← [[classes/media-studies/lesson-plans/9607-s1-lesson-01-the-four-key-concepts|L01]] | [[classes/media-studies/lesson-plans/9607-s1-lesson-03-sign-types-and-codes|L03]] →

## At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| Days | 4 — Mon+Tue two-day block, Wed double, Fri single |
| Dates | Mon 2026-09-07 · Tue 09-08 · Wed 09-09 · Fri 09-11 |
| Band/Unit | U2 Media Language ([[classes/media-studies/unit-plans/9607-s1-unit-2-media-language\|S1 Unit 2]]) |
| AO focus | AO1 |
| Deliverable | CS2 annotated media text from daily life |
| Feeds | A1 |
| Homework | CS2 annotation task (set day 1, 72-hour rule), capped at 30 min per day |

## Objectives

By the end of this lesson, you can:

1. Use signifier, signified, denotation and connotation accurately in an unprompted sentence
2. Identify the assumed audience of a text and cite the address features that prove it
3. Annotate a self-chosen everyday text with at least six accurate code labels (CS2)
4. State your committed media area and one reason it will survive until May

## Goal

This week you take the sign apart and put it back together. Monday names the words you circled in the CS1 exit swap — *worried, poor, desperate* — as **connotation**, and uses Saussure's terms to hold it apart from what the image denotes. Tuesday shows that connotation is cultural, not natural, using EN/ZH examples. Wednesday turns to **address** — who the text thinks you are — and ends with you committing to the media area you will keep feeding until May. Friday names the caption's power — **anchorage** — and collects CS2.

## How it runs

### D1 — Mon 09-07: signifier, signified, and the parked list

- **Starter (5 min)** — the L01 parked list on the board, verbatim. These words were smuggled in; today they get their proper names.
- **Input (15 min)** — from **Deck U2.2**: sign = **signifier** (the form) + **signified** (the idea); **denotation** vs **connotation** on a worked ad reading; **polysemy** — one image, several legitimate readings.
- **Stations (20 min)** — eight images around the room, two columns per image in your sketchpad: *shows* / *suggests*. A "suggests" entry must point at the signifier that triggers it.
- **Close (5 min)** — start your **theory-card spine**: use WS 2.1's card template to make two cards tonight — Saussure and Barthes. Every theorist from now on gets a card; the box stays on the shelf until June. CS2 is set here: an everyday text, ≥6 code labels, 30-minute cap.

### D2 — Tue 09-08: connotation is cultural

- **Retrieval (5 min)** — four questions, no notes: signifier / signified / denotation / connotation.
- **Connotation chains (15 min)** — in pairs, build chains from one signifier (rose → romance → Valentine's → spending), then challenge each link: *who taught you that?*
- **EN/ZH divergence (20 min)** — colors and objects whose connotations split by culture: white (purity / mourning), red (danger / fortune), dragons, the number four. The coursebook color wheel (§2.4) is the frame; the room's two languages are the data. Make lexicon entries on the spot.
- **Written close (5 min)** — using the coursebook §2.1 red-rose frame, write two analytical sentences, one denoting, one connoting, with the connotation traced to its culture.

### D3 — Wed 09-09 (double): modes of address, and the commitment

- **Starter (10 min)** — one advertisement on screen, one question: *how old does this text think you are?* Give evidence.
- **Address profiling (40 min)** — three contrasting texts; in small groups build an **implied-reader profile** for each: age, gender, income, knowledge assumed, mood invited, pronouns used. Groups swap and attack each other's profiles with evidence from the text.
- **Synthesis (20 min)** — formal vs informal address, direct vs indirect; texts don't just find audiences, they *construct* them. Write one paragraph: "This text addresses me as … but I am …"
- **The commitment (15 min)** — log your **committed media area** on the blog with one line of justification. It feeds the L12 case-study document and survives until May. You will not revisit it next week.

### D4 — Fri 09-11: anchorage, and CS2

- **Naming the mechanism (10 min)** — L01's Underwood stereograph returns: the caption that told you who the women were now has a name — **anchorage** (Barthes): text pinning down which of a polysemic image's meanings you take. **Relay**: when words and image take turns carrying the story.
- **Caption swap (15 min)** — one image, three captions written per pair: one anchoring sympathy, one suspicion, one comedy. Read them aloud; the image never changed.
- **CS2 (15 min)** — annotations out, peer-checked against the exemplar (six accurate labels is the bar), then collected.
- **Exit (5 min)** — one sentence: "The most powerful caption I saw this week was … because …"

## Assessment

| Item | Date | What | AO |
|---|---|---|---|
| CS2 | Fri 2026-09-11 | Annotated everyday media text, ≥6 accurate code labels; homework-based, set day 1 (72-hour rule) | AO1 |

Milestone inside: **media area committed Wed 09-09** — feeds the C2 case-study document opened in [[classes/media-studies/lesson-plans/9607-s1-lesson-12-institutions-and-section-a-craft|L12]]. See the [[classes/media-studies/assessments/9607-s1-assessments|full register]].

# 9607 S1 Lesson 03: Sign Types and Codes

[[classes/media-studies/media-studies|Media Studies]] · [[classes/media-studies/unit-plans/9607-s1-unit-2-media-language|Unit 2]] · Lesson 03 of 16 · ← [[classes/media-studies/lesson-plans/9607-s1-lesson-02-semiotics-how-images-mean|L02]] | [[classes/media-studies/lesson-plans/9607-s1-lesson-04-genre-and-camera|L04]] →

## At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| Days | 4 — Mon+Tue two-day block, Wed double, Fri single |
| Dates | Mon 2026-09-14 · Tue 09-15 · Wed 09-16 · Fri 09-18 |
| Band/Unit | U2 Media Language ([[classes/media-studies/unit-plans/9607-s1-unit-2-media-language\|S1 Unit 2]]) |
| AO focus | AO1 |
| Deliverable | CS3 vocabulary quiz, 20 items, 20 min |
| Feeds | A1 |
| Homework | Lexicon revision toward CS3; no new tasks |

## Objectives

By the end of this lesson, you can:

1. Sort unfamiliar signs into icon, index and symbol and defend each placement
2. Name all four code families and give one example of each from a single still
3. Read an unseen TV drama still for three minutes and produce code-labeled observations without prompts
4. Score at least 15 of 20 on CS3, or log the missed terms in the lexicon with corrections

## Goal

This lesson consolidates two weeks of terminology into vocabulary you can use under pressure. Peirce's triad gives a second way to sort signs — *how* a sign means, not just what; the four code families give the analytical checklist you will run on every extract for two years. Wednesday's cold read tests reading a text you have never seen using vocabulary alone; Friday's quiz puts the vocabulary on record.

## How it runs

### D1 — Mon 09-14: Peirce's triad

- **Starter (5 min)** — three images flashed: a portrait, a footprint, a national flag. *All three mean something. Do they mean the same way?*
- **Input (15 min)** — Peirce: **icon** (means by resembling — the portrait), **index** (means by physical trace — the footprint, smoke, a photograph itself), **symbol** (means by convention alone — the flag, a word, a sacred deer). A photograph is the interesting case: an index that looks like an icon.
- **Sorting gallery (20 min)** — twelve signs sorted by *how they mean*, in pairs, disagreements defended: emoji, X-ray, wedding ring, siren, brand logo, thumbprint, crucifix, weather vane… Most signs are blends; the argument is the learning.
- **Close (5 min)** — theory card: Peirce, next to Saussure in the box.

### D2 — Tue 09-15: the four code families

- **Retrieval (5 min)** — icon / index / symbol, one example each, no notes.
- **Input (10 min)** — the two-year checklist: **technical** codes (camera, light, edit), **symbolic** codes (objects, color, gesture, dress), **written** codes (any text in frame), **audio** codes (sound, music, silence). Every extract for the next two years gets run through all four.
- **Mapping (25 min)** — two contrasting stills, all four families mapped on each in table form; then you build your **personal code checklist** — the pocket version you will carry into A1 and, eventually, Paper 2.
- **Close (5 min)** — WS 2.2/2.3 drip begins: five sound terms tonight, five editing terms Thursday, toward CS3.

### D3 — Wed 09-16 (double): the cold read

- **Model (20 min)** — the protocol modeled once, slowly, on one dense image: three minutes of silent noticing, then the four families out loud — where is the light coming from and what does it do; who gestures at whom; what does each garment claim; what text is present *or deliberately absent*; what would this room sound like. The model still is an old master painting: no dialogue, no famous faces, nothing but codes.
- **Cold reads (40 min)** — three unseen TV-drama stills, one at a time: three minutes silent noticing, then a code-labeled write-up per still. No conferring until all three are done.
- **Review (25 min)** — readings compared; **precision beats quantity** — one exact technical observation with its effect outranks five vague ones.
- **Exit (5 min)** — which code family do you reach for first, and which do you forget? Written, kept for A1 prep.

### D4 — Fri 09-18: CS3

- **CS3 (20 min)** — twenty items, twenty minutes: define-the-term and label-the-example.
- **Self-mark (15 min)** — immediate, against definitions on screen; missed terms corrected into the lexicon on the spot.
- **Exit (5 min)** — one term taught back to a partner, partner confirms or corrects.

## Assessment
